s: Dead-simple multithreaded RAM key/value store - the original lookaside cache workhorse.
w: Slab allocator partitions memory into size classes; LRU evicts within slabs. Keys hash across a server ring (clients pick node). No persistence, no replication: a lost node is just a cold cache that refills. Multithreading gives high throughput per box on simple GET/SET workloads.
use: Pure lookaside caching of DB rows/rendered fragments with strict TTLs
Massive GET-heavy read absorption where simplicity wins
Session storage acceptable to lose on reboot (users just re-login)
Multithreaded throughput on few large nodes rather than many Redis shards
avoid: Anything needing persistence, pub/sub, Lua, sorted sets (choose redis)
Cache stampede-sensitive keys without locking strategy (no native CAS-heavy ops ecosystem)
Datasets exceeding RAM comfort - eviction storm risk
world: Facebook/Meta's massive memcached fleet (their NSDI paper is canonical)

pat.d: App reads cache, misses go to DB then populate cache - memcached's bread and butter.

pits: Hot-key saturation of one slab class - spread suffixes or duplicate hot values
Thundering herd on expiry - jitter TTLs, use stale-while-revalidate patterns
Node loss = instant DB load spike - pre-warm replicas or accept degraded SLO briefly
tips: vs Redis question: memcached = simpler+faster multithreaded for pure cache; redis = richer datatypes/persistence/pubsub
